arxiv-2103-01122.title: Multi-fluid hydrodynamics in charge density waves with collective, electronic, and solitonic densities and currents.
arxiv-2103-01122.creator: S.Brazovskii, N.Kirova
arxiv-2103-01122.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by S.Brazovskii, N.Kirova. Abstract

We present a general scheme to approach the space - time evolution of deformations, currents, and the electric field in charge density waves related to appearance of intrinsic topological defects: dislocations, their loops or pairs, and solitons. We derive general equations for the multi-fluid hydrodynamics taking into account the collective mode, electric field, normal electrons, and the intrinsic defects.

arxiv-2504-10163.title: Shoulder Range of Motion Rehabilitation Robot Incorporating Scapulohumeral Rhythm for Frozen Shoulder
arxiv-2504-10163.creator: Hyunbum Cho, Sungmoon Hur, Joowan Kim, Keewon Kim, Jaeheung Park
arxiv-2504-10163.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel rehabilitation robot designed to address the challenges of passive range of motion (PROM) exercises for frozen shoulder patients by integrating advanced scapulohumeral rhythm stabilization. Frozen shoulder is characterized by limited glenohumeral motion and disrupted scapulohumeral rhythm, with therapist-assisted interventions being highly effective for restoring normal shoulder function.

pmc-10587796.title: Nasal Suctioning Therapy Among Infants With Bronchiolitis Discharged Home From the Emergency Department
pmc-10587796.creator: Suzanne Schuh, Allan L. Coates, Judy Sweeney, Maggie Rumantir, Mohamed Eltorki, Waleed Alqurashi, Amy C. Plint, Roger Zemek, Naveen Poonai, Patricia C. Parkin, Diane Soares, Rahim Moineddin, Yaron Finkelstein
pmc-10587796.description: Key PointsQuestionWhat is the effectiveness of enhanced nasal suctioning compared with minimal suctioning in infants with bronchiolitis discharged home from pediatric emergency departments?FindingsIn this randomized clinical trial of 367 infants, minimal bulb suctioning resulted in significantly higher additional resource use compared with enhanced battery-operated suctioning at 72 hours.

pmc-11401396.title: Cleavage of Stau2 by 3C protease promotes EV-A71 replication
pmc-11401396.creator: Hui Li, Jie Song, Zhi Deng, Yunfang Yao, Wentao Qiao, Juan Tan
pmc-11401396.description: BackgroundEnterovirus A71 (EV-A71), as a neurotropic virus, mainly affects infants and young children under the age of 5. EV-A71 infection causes hand-foot-mouth disease and herpetic angina, and even life-threatening neurological complications. However, the molecular mechanism by which EV-A71 induces nervous system damage remains elusive.

pmc-11431005.title: A Hierarchical RF-XGBoost Model for Short-Cycle Agricultural Product Sales Forecasting
pmc-11431005.creator: Jiawen Li, Binfan Lin, Peixian Wang, Yanmei Chen, Xianxian Zeng, Xin Liu, Rongjun Chen
pmc-11431005.description: Short-cycle agricultural product sales forecasting significantly reduces food waste by accurately predicting demand, ensuring producers match supply with consumer needs. However, the forecasting is often subject to uncertain factors, resulting in highly volatile and discontinuous data. To address this, a hierarchical prediction model that combines RF-XGBoost is proposed in this work.

pmc-11479063.creator: Eric Schmid, Tim Oliver Pertzel, Hermann Nirschl, Gisela Guthausen
pmc-11479063.description: Quality control in a production plant shows its maximum potential in the form of inline measurements. Nuclear Magnetic Resonance offers a wide range of applications but requires dedicated adaptation to the respective process and material conditions.

pmc-11695904.title: KPRR: a novel machine learning approach for effectively capturing nonadditive effects in genomic prediction
pmc-11695904.creator: Mianyan Li, Thomas Hall, David E MacHugh, Liang Chen, Dorian Garrick, Lixian Wang, Fuping Zhao
pmc-11695904.description: Nonadditive genetic effects pose significant challenges to traditional genomic selection methods for quantitative traits. Machine learning approaches, particularly kernel-based methods, offer promising solutions to overcome these limitations. In this study, we developed a novel machine learning method, KPRR, which integrated a polynomial kernel into ridge regression to effectively capture nonadditive genetic effects.

pmc-12631541.title: An Integrated Clinical‐Radiomics‐Deep Learning Model Based on 18F‐FDG PET/CT for Predicting EGFR Mutation Status in Lung Adenocarcinoma

pmc-12631541.description: BackgroundAn integrated model combining clinical variables, radiomic features, and deep learning was developed to predict EGFR mutation status in patients with lung adenocarcinoma based on pretreatment 18F‐FDG PET/CT imaging.MethodsIn this retrospective study, data from 218 patients—including PET/CT images, EGFR mutation status, and clinical characteristics—were analyzed.

pmc-13615883.title: Delayed Metal Hypersensitivity from Surgical Clips Causing Progressive Neuropathy
pmc-13615883.creator: Satyamedha Bathula, Oluwasegun J. Olowe, Amanda Lalama, Krystal Virk, Alejandro Pena, Frederick Tiesenga
pmc-13615883.description: Introduction:Systemic immune reactions to surgical clips or implants remain underrecognized and pose a diagnostic challenge after minimally invasive surgeries. Although the incidence of metal hypersensitivity is increasing, these reactions are often overlooked because postoperative imaging and routine evaluations are frequently unremarkable.

pmc-13646032.title: Clinical and genetic features of pediatric hereditary polyposis syndromes in Israel: A nationwide multicenter cohort
pmc-13646032.creator: Shlomi Cohen, Tal Cozacov, Ilana Weintraub, Ron Shaoul, Oren Ledder, Dotan Yogev, Mordechai Slae, Ranya Egbarieh, Galina Ling, Anat Yerushalmy‐Feler
pmc-13646032.description: ObjectivesHereditary polyposis syndromes in children are rare, heterogeneous disorders associated with significant morbidity and long‐term risk of malignancy. Current data on their presentation, management, and outcomes in pediatric populations remain limited.MethodsWe conducted a nationwide, multicenter, retrospective study that included children diagnosed with polyposis syndromes in eight pediatric gastroenterology centers in Israel. Demographic, genetic, clinical, endoscopic, and outcome data were collected.
